# USA Basketball 3x3 at the Olympics

3x3 basketball was featured as an Olympic sport for the first time at the 2020 Tokyo Games (held in 2021). The United States are the only team to medal in multiple Games and made history as the first Olympic 3x3 women’s gold medal winner with a team featuring WNBA players Stefanie Dolson, Allisha Gray, Kelsey Plum and Jackie Young.

# Cierra Burdick

Position(s)**Forward**

Height**6‐2**

Weight**165**

Age**32**

Hometown**Charlotte, NC**

High School**David W. Butler HS**

College**University of Tennessee**

*   Bio 
*   Fiba 5x5 
*   Fiba 3x3 

_**As of Aug. 25, 2025**_

## USA Basketball Notes

*   **Gold Medals:**2023 Pan American Games 3x3, 2023 FIBA 3x3 World Cup, 2014 FIBA 3x3 World Cup, 2011 FIBA U19 World Cup, 2010 FIBA U17 World Cup, 2009 FIBA Americas U16 Championship.
*   **Bronze Medal:**2024 Olympic Games 3x3.
*   **Teams:** 2025 USA 3x3 Women's Series Team; 2024 3x3 Olympic Team; 2025 USA 3x3 Women's Series Team; 2023 USA 3x3 Women's Pan American Games Team; 2023 and 2022 USA 3x3 Women's Series (USA); 2023, 2022 and 2014 USA 3x3 Women's World Cup Team; 2022 USA 3x3 Women's AmeriCup Team; 2011 USA Women's U19 National Team; 2010 USA Women's U17 National Team; 2009 USA Women's U16 National Team.
*   **Honors:** MVP of the 2021 Red Bull USA Basketball 3X Nationals, member of the 2011 USA Basketball Team of the Year.
*   **2025:**
    *   Helped USA to a third-place finish (5-1 record, including a 2-0 mark in the Qualifying Draw) at the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series Bordeaux Stop in Bordeaux, France.
    *   Competed at the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Women’s Series Jakarta Stop in Jakarta, Indonesia. Finished 1-1.
    *   Competed at the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series Marseille Stop in Marseille, France. Finished sixth (4-1) and lost 20-12 to Spain in the quarterfinals.
    *   Named to the 2025 USA 3x3 Women's Series Team (5/21/25).
    *   Played for Team Chaos at the 2025 USA Basketball 3X Nationals May 2-4 in Mesa, Arizona.
    *   Participant at the 2025 USA Basketball 3x3 development camp April 28-30 in Phoenix.

*   **2024:**
    *   Claimed a bronze medal at the 2024 Olympic Games. Ranked second on the team in total key assists (11).
    *   Finished in third place with USA on the Women's Series tour at the Fribourg Stop in Fribourg, Switzerland, from July 4-5, 2024.
    *   Took first place with USA on the Women's Series at the Quebec Stop in Quebec City, Canada, from June 29-30, 2024.
    *   Named to the 2024 USA 3x3 Women's National Team, which will compete at the 2024 Olympic Games Paris (6/5/24).
    *   Helped USA to a second-place finish at the 2024 FIBA 3x3 Women’s Series Springfield Stop.
    *   Participated in the 2024 USA 3x3 Women’s National Team training camp in Springfield, Massachusetts.

*   **2023:**
    *   Helped the 2023 USA 3x3 Women's Pan American Games Team to a 5-0 record and gold in Santiago, Chile, from Oct. 21-23.
    *   Member of the USA roster for the 2023 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series and named to the Women's Series Final roster on September 13, 2023.
    *   Helped the USA 3x3 Women’s Series Final roster finish fourth at the Ulaanbaatar Final, the last stop on the FIBA 3x3 Women’s Series, Sept. 16-17 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.
    *   Represented USA at Poitiers Stop from June 27-28, 2023. The team finished seventh at the stop.
    *   Helped the USA capture first place at Pristina Stop from July 14-15, 2023. She led all players on the stop in player value (36.0), rebounds (37) and key assists (10).
    *   Represented USA at Bordeaux Stop from July 19-20, 2023.
    *   Helped USA to a third-place finish at Edmonton Stop from July 29-30, 2023. Finished third amongst all players in rebounds (26).
    *   Led the USA to their second first-place finish on the Women's Series at Katowice Stop from August 14-15, 2023. She led all players on the stop in total rebounds (37) and finished ranked second in player value (32.4).
    *   Represented the USA at the Melilla Stop from Aug. 18-19, 2023. The team finished in fifth place.
    *   Helped USA to a fourth-place finish at the Montreal Stop from September 2-3, 2023.
    *   Named to the 2023 USA 3x3 Women's World Cup Team (5/18/23).
    *   At the 2023 FIBA 3x3 Women's World Cup, won a gold medal and averaged 3.6 points and 5.6 rebounds (T-second overall) in seven games.

*   **2022:**
    *   Member of the 2022 FIBA 3x3 Women’s Series team.
    *   Competed at the Poitiers Challenger where she averaged 3.6 points and a team-high 5.4 rebounds through five games played. The USA finished second after falling to Germany in the title game.
    *   Member of the 2022 USA Basketball 3x3 World Cup Team, where she averaged 3.6 points through five games.

*   **2021:**
    *   Won a gold medal at the 2021 FIBA 3x3 Women's AmeriCup. Named to the 2021 USA Basketball 3x3 Women's AmeriCup Team (10/25/21).
    *   As a member of the USA roster at the 2021 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series Klaipeda stop, helped the USA to a 5-0 record and the tournament title.
    *   With Force 10 won the title at the 2021 Red Bull USA Basketball 3X Nationals, where she was named tournament MVP.

*   **2020:**
    *   Attended the 2020 USA Basketball 3x3 Olympic Qualifying Tournament training camp (2/7/20).

*   **2014:**
    *   Helped the USA to a gold medal at the 2014 FIBA 3x3 World Cup.
    *   As a member of Takeover, won the title with a 7-0 record at the 2014 USA Basketball 3x3 National Championship in Colorado Springs, Colorado.

*   **2011:**
    *   As a member of the 2011 USA U19 World Cup Team, helped the USA to a 8-1 record and gold medal; started in four of nine games and averaged 5.7 points and 6.0 rebounds.

*   **2010:**
    *   Member of the 2010 USA U17 World Cup Team that posted a perfect 8-0 record in the inaugural FIBA U17 World Championship; averaged 7.6 points and 4.8 rebounds.
    *   Helped the U.S. earn a 2-1 record to capture a pre-U17 World Cup tournament title in Spain against U17 national teams from Australia, Canada and Spain.

*   **2009:**
    *   As a member of the 2009 USA U16 National Team, averaged 6.8 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.6 steals in 16.6 minutes to help the USA capture a 5-0 record and gold medal at the 2009 FIBA Americas U16 Championship; led the USA or tied for a team high with 4 assists versus Puerto Rico and 7 rebounds and 5 steals against Canada.

## Professional Notes

*   Drafted: No. 14 by Los Angeles in 2015.
*   With Force X in 2019, played in the Red Bull 3X Raleigh; Red Bull 3X Houston; Red Bull 3X Seattle; Red Bull 3X Oakland; Red Bull 3X Denver; and the Red Bull 3X Brooklyn.

## College Notes

*   2015 AP All-America honorable mention.
*   2015 NCAA Spokane Regional All-Tournament Team.
*   2015 Coaches All-Southeastern Conference first team.
*   2015 AP All-SEC second team.
*   2015 SEC All-Tournament Team.
*   2015 College Sports Madness All-SEC second team.
*   2015 CoSIDA Academic All-America second team.
*   Played four seasons at the University of Tennessee (2011-12 to 2014-15).
*   Became the 42nd Lady Volunteer to score 1,000 career points at Tennessee.
*   Saw action in 132 games, posted 1072 points, averaged 8.1 points, 1.8 assists and 6.0 rebounds, went 43.0% from the floor, 36.0% from 3-point and 78.4% from the free throw line.

## Personal Notes

*   Born in Charlotte, North Carolina.
*   Great grandfather, Lloyd Burdick, played tackle for the NFL's Chicago Bears from 1931-32.
*   Majored in communication studies.
*   One of five finalists for the 2011 Naismith National High School Player of the Year; 2011 McDonald’s High School All-American; 2011 WBCA High School All-American; 2010 and 2011 Gatorade North Carolina Girls Basketball Player of the Year; 2011 USA Today All-USA first team; 2011 Parade Magazine All-America firs team and 2010 third team; 2011 AP North Carolina Player of the Year 2010 and Co-Player of the Year; 2011 Charlotte Observer North Carolina Ms. Basketball and 2010 Mecklenburg County Co-Player of the Year, 2010 All-Mecklenburg first team and 2009 and 2010 All-State first team.
*   Also participated in track & field, was a 2008 North Carolina 4A outdoor state champion, 2010 North Carolina 4A indoor state champ in the high jump and was the 2011 Butler High School Field MVP.

# Cierra Burdick

Position(s)**Forward**

Height**6‐2**

Weight**165**

Age**32**

Hometown**Charlotte, NC**

High School**David W. Butler HS**

College**University of Tennessee**

*   Bio 
*   Fiba 5x5 
*   Fiba 3x3 

_**As of Aug. 25, 2025**_

## USA Basketball Notes

*   **Gold Medals:**2023 Pan American Games 3x3, 2023 FIBA 3x3 World Cup, 2014 FIBA 3x3 World Cup, 2011 FIBA U19 World Cup, 2010 FIBA U17 World Cup, 2009 FIBA Americas U16 Championship.
*   **Bronze Medal:**2024 Olympic Games 3x3.
*   **Teams:** 2025 USA 3x3 Women's Series Team; 2024 3x3 Olympic Team; 2025 USA 3x3 Women's Series Team; 2023 USA 3x3 Women's Pan American Games Team; 2023 and 2022 USA 3x3 Women's Series (USA); 2023, 2022 and 2014 USA 3x3 Women's World Cup Team; 2022 USA 3x3 Women's AmeriCup Team; 2011 USA Women's U19 National Team; 2010 USA Women's U17 National Team; 2009 USA Women's U16 National Team.
*   **Honors:** MVP of the 2021 Red Bull USA Basketball 3X Nationals, member of the 2011 USA Basketball Team of the Year.
*   **2025:**
    *   Helped USA to a third-place finish (5-1 record, including a 2-0 mark in the Qualifying Draw) at the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series Bordeaux Stop in Bordeaux, France.
    *   Competed at the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Women’s Series Jakarta Stop in Jakarta, Indonesia. Finished 1-1.
    *   Competed at the 2025 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series Marseille Stop in Marseille, France. Finished sixth (4-1) and lost 20-12 to Spain in the quarterfinals.
    *   Named to the 2025 USA 3x3 Women's Series Team (5/21/25).
    *   Played for Team Chaos at the 2025 USA Basketball 3X Nationals May 2-4 in Mesa, Arizona.
    *   Participant at the 2025 USA Basketball 3x3 development camp April 28-30 in Phoenix.

*   **2024:**
    *   Claimed a bronze medal at the 2024 Olympic Games. Ranked second on the team in total key assists (11).
    *   Finished in third place with USA on the Women's Series tour at the Fribourg Stop in Fribourg, Switzerland, from July 4-5, 2024.
    *   Took first place with USA on the Women's Series at the Quebec Stop in Quebec City, Canada, from June 29-30, 2024.
    *   Named to the 2024 USA 3x3 Women's National Team, which will compete at the 2024 Olympic Games Paris (6/5/24).
    *   Helped USA to a second-place finish at the 2024 FIBA 3x3 Women’s Series Springfield Stop.
    *   Participated in the 2024 USA 3x3 Women’s National Team training camp in Springfield, Massachusetts.

*   **2023:**
    *   Helped the 2023 USA 3x3 Women's Pan American Games Team to a 5-0 record and gold in Santiago, Chile, from Oct. 21-23.
    *   Member of the USA roster for the 2023 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series and named to the Women's Series Final roster on September 13, 2023.
    *   Helped the USA 3x3 Women’s Series Final roster finish fourth at the Ulaanbaatar Final, the last stop on the FIBA 3x3 Women’s Series, Sept. 16-17 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia.
    *   Represented USA at Poitiers Stop from June 27-28, 2023. The team finished seventh at the stop.
    *   Helped the USA capture first place at Pristina Stop from July 14-15, 2023. She led all players on the stop in player value (36.0), rebounds (37) and key assists (10).
    *   Represented USA at Bordeaux Stop from July 19-20, 2023.
    *   Helped USA to a third-place finish at Edmonton Stop from July 29-30, 2023. Finished third amongst all players in rebounds (26).
    *   Led the USA to their second first-place finish on the Women's Series at Katowice Stop from August 14-15, 2023. She led all players on the stop in total rebounds (37) and finished ranked second in player value (32.4).
    *   Represented the USA at the Melilla Stop from Aug. 18-19, 2023. The team finished in fifth place.
    *   Helped USA to a fourth-place finish at the Montreal Stop from September 2-3, 2023.
    *   Named to the 2023 USA 3x3 Women's World Cup Team (5/18/23).
    *   At the 2023 FIBA 3x3 Women's World Cup, won a gold medal and averaged 3.6 points and 5.6 rebounds (T-second overall) in seven games.

*   **2022:**
    *   Member of the 2022 FIBA 3x3 Women’s Series team.
    *   Competed at the Poitiers Challenger where she averaged 3.6 points and a team-high 5.4 rebounds through five games played. The USA finished second after falling to Germany in the title game.
    *   Member of the 2022 USA Basketball 3x3 World Cup Team, where she averaged 3.6 points through five games.

*   **2021:**
    *   Won a gold medal at the 2021 FIBA 3x3 Women's AmeriCup. Named to the 2021 USA Basketball 3x3 Women's AmeriCup Team (10/25/21).
    *   As a member of the USA roster at the 2021 FIBA 3x3 Women's Series Klaipeda stop, helped the USA to a 5-0 record and the tournament title.
    *   With Force 10 won the title at the 2021 Red Bull USA Basketball 3X Nationals, where she was named tournament MVP.

*   **2020:**
    *   Attended the 2020 USA Basketball 3x3 Olympic Qualifying Tournament training camp (2/7/20).

*   **2014:**
    *   Helped the USA to a gold medal at the 2014 FIBA 3x3 World Cup.
    *   As a member of Takeover, won the title with a 7-0 record at the 2014 USA Basketball 3x3 National Championship in Colorado Springs, Colorado.

*   **2011:**
    *   As a member of the 2011 USA U19 World Cup Team, helped the USA to a 8-1 record and gold medal; started in four of nine games and averaged 5.7 points and 6.0 rebounds.

*   **2010:**
    *   Member of the 2010 USA U17 World Cup Team that posted a perfect 8-0 record in the inaugural FIBA U17 World Championship; averaged 7.6 points and 4.8 rebounds.
    *   Helped the U.S. earn a 2-1 record to capture a pre-U17 World Cup tournament title in Spain against U17 national teams from Australia, Canada and Spain.

*   **2009:**
    *   As a member of the 2009 USA U16 National Team, averaged 6.8 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.6 steals in 16.6 minutes to help the USA capture a 5-0 record and gold medal at the 2009 FIBA Americas U16 Championship; led the USA or tied for a team high with 4 assists versus Puerto Rico and 7 rebounds and 5 steals against Canada.

## Professional Notes

*   Drafted: No. 14 by Los Angeles in 2015.
*   With Force X in 2019, played in the Red Bull 3X Raleigh; Red Bull 3X Houston; Red Bull 3X Seattle; Red Bull 3X Oakland; Red Bull 3X Denver; and the Red Bull 3X Brooklyn.

## College Notes

*   2015 AP All-America honorable mention.
*   2015 NCAA Spokane Regional All-Tournament Team.
*   2015 Coaches All-Southeastern Conference first team.
*   2015 AP All-SEC second team.
*   2015 SEC All-Tournament Team.
*   2015 College Sports Madness All-SEC second team.
*   2015 CoSIDA Academic All-America second team.
*   Played four seasons at the University of Tennessee (2011-12 to 2014-15).
*   Became the 42nd Lady Volunteer to score 1,000 career points at Tennessee.
*   Saw action in 132 games, posted 1072 points, averaged 8.1 points, 1.8 assists and 6.0 rebounds, went 43.0% from the floor, 36.0% from 3-point and 78.4% from the free throw line.

## Personal Notes

*   Born in Charlotte, North Carolina.
*   Great grandfather, Lloyd Burdick, played tackle for the NFL's Chicago Bears from 1931-32.
*   Majored in communication studies.
*   One of five finalists for the 2011 Naismith National High School Player of the Year; 2011 McDonald’s High School All-American; 2011 WBCA High School All-American; 2010 and 2011 Gatorade North Carolina Girls Basketball Player of the Year; 2011 USA Today All-USA first team; 2011 Parade Magazine All-America firs team and 2010 third team; 2011 AP North Carolina Player of the Year 2010 and Co-Player of the Year; 2011 Charlotte Observer North Carolina Ms. Basketball and 2010 Mecklenburg County Co-Player of the Year, 2010 All-Mecklenburg first team and 2009 and 2010 All-State first team.
*   Also participated in track & field, was a 2008 North Carolina 4A outdoor state champion, 2010 North Carolina 4A indoor state champ in the high jump and was the 2011 Butler High School Field MVP.

## USA Basketball Notes

*   **Gold Medal:** 2023 FIBA 3x3 AmeriCup.
*   **Bronze Medal:**2024 Olympic Games 3x3.
*   **Teams:**2026 USA Women's World Cup Qualifying Team, 2024 USA 3x3 Women's Olympic Team, 2023 USA 3x3 Women's AmeriCup Team, 2023 USA Women's National Team, 2022 USA Women's World Cup Qualifying Team.
*   **Honors:**2023 FIBA 3x3 AmeriCup MVP.
*   **2026**
    *   As a member of the 2026 USA Women’s World Cup Qualifying Team, helped the team to a 5-0 record while averaging 6.8 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.4 assists in five games.

*   **2025:**
    *   Participated in the December 2025 Women's National Team Training Camp in Durham, North Carolina.

*   **2024:**
    *   Claimed a bronze medal at the 2024 Olympic Games. Led the team in rebounds (44, 4.9 rpg), 1-point shooting percentage (57%, 31-54). Ranked second on the team in scoring (37, 4.1 ppg).
    *   Named to the 2024 USA 3x3 Women's National Team, which will compete at the 2024 Olympic Games Paris (6/24/24).
    *   Captured a fourth-place finish with Springfield at the 2024 FIBA 3x3 Women’s Series Springfield Stop.
    *   Participated in the 2024 USA 3x3 Women’s National Team training camp in Springfield, Massachusetts.

*   **2023:**
    *   Claimed MVP honors and helped the USA to gold at the 2023 FIBA 3x3 AmeriCup in San Juan, Puerto Rico, after leading the team in scoring (6.6 ppg), total key assists (10) and rebounding (7.0 rpg).
    *   Hit the game-winning shot as time expired in the gold medal game to seal the win over Brazil. The team trailed 13-19 with two minutes to play and won 21-20.
    *   Named to the 2023 USA Women's 3x3 AmeriCup Team (11/27/23).
    *   Invited to the 2023 USA Women’s National Team November training camp in Atlanta and played in the USA-Duke exhibition Nov. 12 in Durham, North Carolina.

*   **2022:**
    *   Invited to attend 2022 USA Basketball Women’s National Team training camp in Las Vegas but did not attend due to WNBA Playoffs.
    *   Participated in the 2022 USA National Team's spring minicamp in Minneapolis.
    *   Member of the 2022 USA World Cup Qualifying Team; averaged 9.5 points and 4.5 rebounds in helping the USA to a 2-0 mark against Belgium and Puerto Rico.
    *   Made USA Basketball debut at 2022 USA National Team’s February training camp.

## Professional Notes

*   Averaged a career-best 18.4 points on 57.2% from the floor during the 2025 season with the Sparks.
*   Has played 11 WNBA seasons with San Antonio, Las Vegas and Los Angeles.
*   Selected No. 6 overall by San Antonio in 2015.
*   To visit Hamby’s WNBA bio, click [here](https://www.wnba.com/player/204324/dearica-hamby).

## College Notes

*   Attended Wake Forest University (2011-12 through 2014-15), capping career as Wake Forest's all-time leading scorer (1,801 pts) and rebounder (1,021 rebs).
*   Among numerous honors, named Wake Forest’s 2015 Female Student-Athlete of the Year (Marge Crisp Award) and two-time All-ACC first team (2014-15).

## Personal Notes

*   Has two children, Amaya and Legend.
*   Daughter of Carla Hamby and Derrick Jones; has two sisters, Chelsie and Desaraye.
*   Helped lead Norcross High School (Georgia) to a 5-A state title in 2011; attended Marietta High School her first three years.
*   Was also a standout on the softball field.
*   Instagram: [@dearicamarie](https://www.instagram.com/dearicamarie/)

## USA Basketball Notes

*   **Gold Medal:** 2023 FIBA 3x3 AmeriCup.
*   **Bronze Medal:**2024 Olympic Games 3x3.
*   **Teams:**2026 USA Women's World Cup Qualifying Team, 2024 USA 3x3 Women's Olympic Team, 2023 USA 3x3 Women's AmeriCup Team, 2023 USA Women's National Team, 2022 USA Women's World Cup Qualifying Team.

*   **2026**
    *   As a member of the 2026 USA Women’s World Cup Qualifying Team, helped the team to a 5-0 record while averaging 6.8 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.4 assists in five games.

*   **2025:**
    *   Participated in the December 2025 Women's National Team Training Camp in Durham, North Carolina.

*   **2024:**
    *   Claimed a bronze medal at the 2024 Olympic Games. Led the team in rebounds (44, 4.9 rpg), 1-point shooting percentage (57%, 31-54). Ranked second on the team in scoring (37, 4.1 ppg).
    *   Named to the 2024 USA 3x3 Women's National Team, which will compete at the 2024 Olympic Games Paris (6/24/24).
    *   Captured a fourth-place finish with Springfield at the 2024 FIBA 3x3 Women’s Series Springfield Stop.
    *   Participated in the 2024 USA 3x3 Women’s National Team training camp in Springfield, Massachusetts.

*   **2023:**
    *   Claimed MVP honors and helped the USA to gold at the 2023 FIBA 3x3 AmeriCup in San Juan, Puerto Rico, after leading the team in scoring (6.6 ppg), total key assists (10) and rebounding (7.0 rpg).
    *   Hit the game-winning shot as time expired in the gold medal game to seal the win over Brazil. The team trailed 13-19 with two minutes to play and won 21-20.
    *   Named to the 2023 USA Women's 3x3 AmeriCup Team (11/27/23).
    *   Invited to the 2023 USA Women’s National Team November training camp in Atlanta and played in the USA-Duke exhibition Nov. 12 in Durham, North Carolina.

*   **2022:**
    *   Invited to attend 2022 USA Basketball Women’s National Team training camp in Las Vegas but did not attend due to WNBA Playoffs.
    *   Participated in the 2022 USA National Team's spring minicamp in Minneapolis.
    *   Member of the 2022 USA World Cup Qualifying Team; averaged 9.5 points and 4.5 rebounds in helping the USA to a 2-0 mark against Belgium and Puerto Rico.
    *   Made USA Basketball debut at 2022 USA National Team’s February training camp.

## Professional Notes

*   Averaged a career-best 18.4 points on 57.2% from the floor during the 2025 season with the Sparks.
*   Has played 11 WNBA seasons with San Antonio, Las Vegas and Los Angeles.
*   Selected No. 6 overall by San Antonio in 2015.
*   To visit Hamby’s WNBA bio, click [here](https://www.wnba.com/player/204324/dearica-hamby).

## College Notes

*   Attended Wake Forest University (2011-12 through 2014-15), capping career as Wake Forest's all-time leading scorer (1,801 pts) and rebounder (1,021 rebs).
*   Among numerous honors, named Wake Forest’s 2015 Female Student-Athlete of the Year (Marge Crisp Award) and two-time All-ACC first team (2014-15).

## Personal Notes

*   Has two children, Amaya and Legend.
*   Daughter of Carla Hamby and Derrick Jones; has two sisters, Chelsie and Desaraye.
*   Helped lead Norcross High School (Georgia) to a 5-A state title in 2011; attended Marietta High School her first three years.
*   Was also a standout on the softball field.

The **2022–23 Tennessee Lady Volunteers basketball team** represented the [University of Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tennessee "University of Tennessee") in the [2022–23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season")[college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") season. Led by former Lady Vol [Kellie Harper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kellie_Harper "Kellie Harper"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-1) entering her fourth year as head coach, the team played its games at [Thompson–Boling Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thompson%E2%80%93Boling_Arena "Thompson–Boling Arena") as members of the [Southeastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference "Southeastern Conference").

The Lady Vols finished the season with a 25–12 overall record, 13–3 in the conference. They advanced to the finals of the [SEC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_SEC_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 SEC women's basketball tournament"), where they lost to South Carolina.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-2) Finishing strong in the conference, the Lady Vols earned an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"), advancing to the Sweet Sixteen before losing to Virginia Tech.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-3)

## Previous season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Previous season")]

The [2021–22 team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team "2021–22 Tennessee Lady Volunteers basketball team") finished the season 25–9, 11–5 in third place in SEC play. They lost in the semifinals of the [SEC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_SEC_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 SEC women's basketball tournament") to their rivals, Kentucky,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-4) who went on to win the tournament. The Lady Vols also received an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"), where they lost in the Sweet Sixteen to Louisville.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-5)

The **2022–23 Tennessee Lady Volunteers basketball team** represented the [University of Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Tennessee "University of Tennessee") in the [2022–23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season")[college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") season. Led by former Lady Vol [Kellie Harper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kellie_Harper "Kellie Harper"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-1) entering her fourth year as head coach, the team played its games at [Thompson–Boling Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thompson%E2%80%93Boling_Arena "Thompson–Boling Arena") as members of the [Southeastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference "Southeastern Conference").

The Lady Vols finished the season with a 25–12 overall record, 13–3 in the conference. They advanced to the finals of the [SEC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_SEC_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 SEC women's basketball tournament"), where they lost to South Carolina.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-2) Finishing strong in the conference, the Lady Vols earned an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"), advancing to the Sweet Sixteen before losing to Virginia Tech.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-3)

## Previous season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Previous season")]

The [2021–22 team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team "2021–22 Tennessee Lady Volunteers basketball team") finished the season 25–9, 11–5 in third place in SEC play. They lost in the semifinals of the [SEC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_SEC_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 SEC women's basketball tournament") to their rivals, Kentucky,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-4) who went on to win the tournament. The Lady Vols also received an at-large bid to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament"), where they lost in the Sweet Sixteen to Louisville.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Tennessee_Lady_Volunteers_basketball_team#cite_note-5)

The **2022–23 Wake Forest Demon Deacons women's basketball team** represented [Wake Forest University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Forest_University "Wake Forest University") during the [2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season"). The Demon Deacons were led by first-year head coach [Megan Gebbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megan_Gebbia "Megan Gebbia"), competed as members of the [Atlantic Coast Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Coast_Conference "Atlantic Coast Conference") and played their home games at the [Lawrence Joel Veterans Memorial Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Joel_Veterans_Memorial_Coliseum "Lawrence Joel Veterans Memorial Coliseum").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-3)

Prior to the season, Wake Forest fired head coach [Jen Hoover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jen_Hoover "Jen Hoover") after ten seasons.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-4)[Megan Gebbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megan_Gebbia "Megan Gebbia") was announced as the new head coach on May 26, 2022.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-5)

The Demon Deacons finished the season 17–17 overall and 5–13 in [ACC play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Atlantic_Coast_Conference_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference women's basketball season") to finish in a tie for eleventh place. As the twelfth seed in the [ACC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_ACC_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 ACC women's basketball tournament"), they defeated thirteenth seed [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Virginia_Cavaliers_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Virginia Cavaliers women's basketball team") in the First Round and fifth seed [Florida State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Florida_State_Seminoles_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Florida State Seminoles women's basketball team") in the Second Round before losing to fourth seed [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Louisville_Cardinals_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Louisville Cardinals women's basketball team") in the Quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [WNIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Women's_National_Invitation_Tournament "2023 Women's National Invitation Tournament"). They defeated [Morgan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_State_Bears_women's_basketball "Morgan State Bears women's basketball") in the First Round before losing to [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Florida_Gators_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Florida Gators women's basketball team") in the Second Round to end their season.

The **2022–23 Wake Forest Demon Deacons women's basketball team** represented [Wake Forest University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Forest_University "Wake Forest University") during the [2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season"). The Demon Deacons were led by first-year head coach [Megan Gebbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megan_Gebbia "Megan Gebbia"), competed as members of the [Atlantic Coast Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Coast_Conference "Atlantic Coast Conference") and played their home games at the [Lawrence Joel Veterans Memorial Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawrence_Joel_Veterans_Memorial_Coliseum "Lawrence Joel Veterans Memorial Coliseum").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-3)

Prior to the season, Wake Forest fired head coach [Jen Hoover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jen_Hoover "Jen Hoover") after ten seasons.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-4)[Megan Gebbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Megan_Gebbia "Megan Gebbia") was announced as the new head coach on May 26, 2022.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Wake_Forest_Demon_Deacons_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-5)

The Demon Deacons finished the season 17–17 overall and 5–13 in [ACC play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Atlantic_Coast_Conference_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 Atlantic Coast Conference women's basketball season") to finish in a tie for eleventh place. As the twelfth seed in the [ACC tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_ACC_women's_basketball_tournament "2023 ACC women's basketball tournament"), they defeated thirteenth seed [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Virginia_Cavaliers_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Virginia Cavaliers women's basketball team") in the First Round and fifth seed [Florida State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Florida_State_Seminoles_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Florida State Seminoles women's basketball team") in the Second Round before losing to fourth seed [Louisville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Louisville_Cardinals_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Louisville Cardinals women's basketball team") in the Quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [WNIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Women's_National_Invitation_Tournament "2023 Women's National Invitation Tournament"). They defeated [Morgan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_State_Bears_women's_basketball "Morgan State Bears women's basketball") in the First Round before losing to [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Florida_Gators_women's_basketball_team "2022–23 Florida Gators women's basketball team") in the Second Round to end their season.

The **2022–23 TCU Horned Frogs women's basketball team** represented [Texas Christian University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Christian_University "Texas Christian University") in the [2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season"). The 2021–22 season was head coach [Raegan Pebley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raegan_Pebley "Raegan Pebley")'s ninth season at TCU. The Horned Frogs are members of the [Big 12 Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_12_Conference "Big 12 Conference") and played their home games in [Schollmaier Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schollmaier_Arena "Schollmaier Arena").

## Previous season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_TCU_Horned_Frogs_women%27s_basketball_team&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Previous season")]

The Horned Frogs finished the season 6–22, 2–16 in Big 12 play to finish in tenth place. In the [Big 12 Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Big_12_Conference_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 Big 12 Conference women's basketball tournament"), they lost to [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_West_Virginia_Mountaineers_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 West Virginia Mountaineers women's basketball team") in the first round. They were not invited to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament") or the [WNIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Women's_National_Invitation_Tournament "2022 Women's National Invitation Tournament").

The **2022–23 TCU Horned Frogs women's basketball team** represented [Texas Christian University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Christian_University "Texas Christian University") in the [2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season"). The 2021–22 season was head coach [Raegan Pebley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raegan_Pebley "Raegan Pebley")'s ninth season at TCU. The Horned Frogs are members of the [Big 12 Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_12_Conference "Big 12 Conference") and played their home games in [Schollmaier Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schollmaier_Arena "Schollmaier Arena").

## Previous season

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022%E2%80%9323_TCU_Horned_Frogs_women%27s_basketball_team&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Previous season")]

The Horned Frogs finished the season 6–22, 2–16 in Big 12 play to finish in tenth place. In the [Big 12 Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Big_12_Conference_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 Big 12 Conference women's basketball tournament"), they lost to [West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_West_Virginia_Mountaineers_women's_basketball_team "2021–22 West Virginia Mountaineers women's basketball team") in the first round. They were not invited to the [NCAA tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_tournament "2022 NCAA Division I women's basketball tournament") or the [WNIT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Women's_National_Invitation_Tournament "2022 Women's National Invitation Tournament").

The **2022–23 Kentucky Wildcats women's basketball team** represented the [University of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kentucky "University of Kentucky") (UK) in the [2022–23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season")[college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") season. Led by third-year head coach [Kyra Elzy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyra_Elzy "Kyra Elzy"), the Wildcats played home games at [Memorial Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_Coliseum_(University_of_Kentucky) "Memorial Coliseum (University of Kentucky)") as members of the [Southeastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference "Southeastern Conference").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Kentucky_Wildcats_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Kentucky_Wildcats_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-2)

The **2022–23 Kentucky Wildcats women's basketball team** represented the [University of Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kentucky "University of Kentucky") (UK) in the [2022–23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NCAA_Division_I_women's_basketball_season "2022–23 NCAA Division I women's basketball season")[college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") season. Led by third-year head coach [Kyra Elzy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyra_Elzy "Kyra Elzy"), the Wildcats played home games at [Memorial Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_Coliseum_(University_of_Kentucky) "Memorial Coliseum (University of Kentucky)") as members of the [Southeastern Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference "Southeastern Conference").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Kentucky_Wildcats_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_Kentucky_Wildcats_women's_basketball_team#cite_note-2)
